defaults.permitted_development: Across Northumberland, for a house, the usual planning route for a driveway is easiest where the work is just hard surfacing inside the plot and run-off from any front area over 5 square metres is dealt with on site. Permission issues often arise from the access, walls or drainage details rather than the parking space alone. That fallback can disappear where an Article 4 direction or an old planning condition has removed the normal householder right.

rules.height_rules: Across Northumberland, retaining or terracing works may need planning permission even where the surfacing material itself would not.
rules.depth_rules: Across Northumberland, the main national control is drainage rather than projection from the house. Shallow or awkward parking layouts can still fail in practice if they leave vehicles overhanging the footway or create poor manoeuvring.
rules.boundary_rules: Across Northumberland, separate highway approval is commonly needed for a new or altered vehicular access.
rules.roof_rules: Across Northumberland, covered parking or shelter features should not be assumed to fall within the same route as the paving.
rules.materials_rules: Across Northumberland, material choice matters most on run-off. Gravel, permeable block paving, porous asphalt or a layout that drains into soft ground are usually easier to justify than impermeable paving that sheds water towards the road.

restrictions.conservation_area: Conservation area status makes driveway schemes more sensitive where front gardens, walls, railings or traditional paving contribute to the street scene.
restrictions.listed_building: Listed building consent may be needed where driveway works alter the setting or fabric of a listed building, including boundary features and historic surfacing.
restrictions.article4_notes: Where Article 4 directions or planning conditions bite, a driveway that would usually fall within householder rights can still need planning permission.
